subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a chibi-style axolotl design: big head, short stubby body, finned tail, four legs with digits, feathery gill branches on each side, and expressive eyes with a smile. I'm settling on realistic proportions scaled to roughly 0.3m length and 0.1m height, working in meters.

I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy -- hips at the root, with a spine chain running to a neck and head joint, plus separate chains for the jaw, tail, legs, and gills -- and mapping out approximate coordinates for the body, head, and tail with a dorsal fin membrane sweeping along the top. I'm sticking to well-known API calls like joint, chain, and sweep to keep things robust and avoid errors.

Still working out model-space positions...

Still working out the smile placement...

For the eyes, I'll position them toward the top sides of the head, bigger than real axolotl eyes for a chibi look—small black spheres with white highlights placed at specific points on the head's surface.

Now I'm adding cheek blush as flat pink discs stuck onto the surface, computed using the same angular placement method with guards for null hits, then moving on to placing three gills per side along the head's sides.

Still writing gill geometry...

I'm thinking about fanning the frills with a third normal direction and alternating pink to rose tip colors for variety, then moving to sweep the body along the spine path using an elliptical radius function.

For the skeleton, I'll build a spine chain from the hips parented forward with two bones, and a separate tail chain with four bones curving backward and down, then combine them into one continuous catmull path from tail tip to head to drive the skinned body sweep.

Working out the tail taper -- making it laterally compressed like an axolotl's tail, with rx smaller than ry shrinking toward the tip, plus matching the radius at the hip seam so the body and tail segments blend smoothly.

Now I'm defining the tail fin as a wavy scalloped outline along the top and bottom of the tail, extruded as a single leaf-shaped membrane covering the whole tail length from the hip out to the tip.

I notice the fin bottom would dip below the floor, so I'm clamping those values and adjusting the bottom tail points to stay within bounds. I'll keep the fin coloring simple rather than adding extra layered extrudes for shading.

Setting the palette now: pale pink body, pink gills, darker speckle accents, and dark eyes for a leucistic axolotl look. I'm also working out the tail fin extrude orientation and starting to plan a low dorsal crest running along the back.

Figuring out where to position the dorsal fin so it only pokes above the body's existing curve instead of clipping through it — adjusting the starting z-coordinate so the fin profile sits just above the surface height.

Now I'm mapping the fin's outline along the tail, extending points from the body to the tail tip with a tapering top edge and a hidden bottom edge, then moving on to designing stubby legs with four toes on the front feet and five on the hind feet.

For the legs, I'm working out shoulder-to-foot positions and distances for front and hind limbs, then choosing two-segment lengths and bend directions so the elbow joint angles outward and back realistically given the geometry.

Now I'm naming the limb chain joints, setting the sweep radii, and building the foot as a flat paddle with four fanned toes using rods with rounded ends, positioning them outward and forward from the foot base.

I'm checking the vertical placement of the foot pad and body so all contact points touch the floor without sinking in. Now I'm positioning the hind legs with shoulder and foot coordinates, and planning the hind toes to fan outward and backward differently from the front ones.

Next I'm attaching head joints, gill bones, and frills, then scattering speckle details across the body and head surfaces using a sweep with minimum distance spacing. I'm also adding pale belly sectors along the body and tail, plus cheek blush discs and nostril details on the head.

For the eyes, I'm placing black eyeball spheres with small white highlights and a slightly darker pink rim ring, then checking their positions against the gill base coordinates to make sure they don't overlap, adjusting the gill base location slightly to keep it within bounds.

Working out the three gill stalks now: setting base offsets, tip positions, and stalk lengths for a frilly chibi look, with the fan plane oriented roughly perpendicular to the z-axis so the gills splay outward.

Now I'm computing the frond direction vectors for each stalk, blending side, tangent, and z components with decreasing length toward the tips, giving each stalk around seven small spikes plus a tip spike -- roughly 90 spikes total across six stalks. I'm also setting up the spine joint chain and parenting structure, figuring out how many intermediate points the path needs.

Still defining joint positions...

Simplifying: I'll just set the body bone to spine, with the tail using a separate chain. For radii, I'm giving the body a bulge profile and defining belly sectors, then matching the tail's starting radius to the body's radius at the hip boundary.

Checking the head-to-body overlap at the neck junction, I confirm the rounded body cap stays hidden inside the head geometry so the connection looks seamless. Now I'm writing the mirrored limb loops, naming the left-side variants with an "L" suffix, and starting a toe-fan helper function.

Writing the toe/rod helper code...
